key_insight: A data-free graph neural network can solve PDEs in solid mechanics by enforcing the weak form with finite-element shape-function gradients instead of automatic differentiation.
engineering_relevance: This enables scalable surrogate solvers for arbitrary geometries and unseen load cases while avoiding the cost of generating and storing high-fidelity training data.
method: Graph neural network with message passing predicts nodal displacements.
Residuals are computed from the weak form using polynomial FEM shape-function gradients.
Residual-based error checking can trigger refinement at inference time.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports residual convergence errors below 1% and claims generalization to unseen load cases and geometries on models of considerable size.
watch_item: Performance still depends on a suitable FEM discretization and reliable residual tolerance settings for inference-time refinement.
paper_title: Data-free neural PDE solvers based on Graph Neural Networks and weak forms
